A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same translation-calibration research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original Tower and ALMA translation experiments, quality-estimation evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and English-to-Chinese human-evaluation results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds an English-to-Russian human-evaluation summary in Appendix H.3, Figure 7.

M1.justification: Both versions minimize negative Pearson correlation between hypothesis log-likelihoods and quality scores, together with SFT on the highest-scoring samples. Nucleus sampling and the on-policy/off-policy alternatives remain unchanged. V3's notation, sampling-distribution explanation, and gradient details do not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Flores-200 training, NTREX validation, WMT22/WMT24 translation evaluation, WMT22 quality estimation, and the represented language directions are retained. English-to-Russian human evaluation was already described in v1 Section 6.2; v3 supplies its results rather than introducing a new task or population.

E2.justification: V3 adds CometKiwi reference comparisons to the English-to-German and English-to-Russian Kendall plots, Figures 9–10; the corresponding v1 Figures 7–8 lack them. CometKiwi already appeared in the Spearman comparisons. The translation and human-evaluation comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 4 changes the CPO baseline label from ALMA-13B-R to ALMA-7B-R, correcting the reported model size. Both versions' accompanying prose already identifies ALMA-7B-R, and the scores are identical, so this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Other training, sampling, validation, and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: The cross-metric study, sampling-size sensitivity analysis, beam-search versus Best-of-N comparison, model-size/training-data analyses, and Chinese annotation-transition analysis are retained. The new Russian evaluation summary adds benchmark evidence without introducing a new ablation, robustness test, or error-analysis design.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-score, correlation, and human-rating reporting practices. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its discussion of nucleus-sampling bias concerns the training objective rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical scores in Tables 1–7 are unchanged. V3 Figure 7 newly reports Russian human ratings: baseline 4.79 versus calibrated 5.21, with 93 wins, 44 losses, and 63 ties over 200 annotations; v1 Appendix D.3 deferred these results. V3 also adds CometKiwi reference results to the Kendall plots.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces v1's integral lacking an explicit sampling measure with covariance and correlation defined through expectations under a distribution. V3 also explicitly formulates the sampled loss under the nucleus-induced distribution and acknowledges its bias. This is a limited formal correction; Appendix C.1's dot-product expansion restates the existing loss rather than introducing a new theorem.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain improved translation through Pearson-based calibration, quality estimation using the same model's likelihoods, and more effective efficient MAP decoding. The revised abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain these claims and their principal comparisons.

C2.justification: New Appendices A–B explicitly delimit evidence to approximate MAP decoding, acknowledge untested exact decoding and very large beams, and restrict demonstrated language applicability to the base models. Section 3 acknowledges sampling bias, Section 5.2 qualifies SFT calibration gains across languages, and Section 5.1 presents full-set SFT degradation as an expectation rather than an unqualified finding.

D1.justification: V3 specifies gradient propagation through log-likelihoods, their mean, and standard deviation, and explains that human-evaluation blinding used shuffled translation-pair order. It also explicitly extends the beam-size-five description to all non-closed-source comparison results. Hyperparameters, hardware, prompt templates, and access links remain unchanged; the base-model pretraining description is shortened.

R1.justification: V3 removes the Background paragraph on translation uncertainty and its references to Galley et al. (2015) and Huang et al. (2024). The remaining bibliography and the main positioning against quality-aware decoding and preference optimization are retained.

P1.justification: V3 streamlines the introduction, background, results discussion, and conclusion, expands the Pearson explanation, merges the base-model and data subsections, and moves prompt templates ahead of supplementary results. The main section sequence and overall argument remain intact. It also corrects the author name from Chritof to Christof Monz.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 3 is placed beside its discussion, and appendix figures and tables are regrouped. V3 adds the Russian human-evaluation figure and CometKiwi lines to the Kendall plots, with expanded captions. Most existing displays retain their structure and plotted results.

improvement.justification: V3 improves methodological clarity through explicit sampling-distribution mathematics and implementation details, adds direct Russian human-evaluation evidence, and states meaningful limits on decoding and language applicability. These address identifiable weaknesses in v1 while preserving its central experiments. The gains are limited: benchmark tables remain unchanged, and some human-evaluation directions promised in the appendix still lack reported results.
